content:
In FPIL where abbreviations are introduced an abbreviation is used for Nat

Finally, defining the new name for Nat using abbrev instead of def allows overloading resolution to replace the defined name with its definition. Definitions written using abbrev are always unfolded. For instance,

abbrev N : Type := Nat
def thirtyNine : N := 39

I find this example confusing since it seems to me that the reason we are using an abbrev instead of a def is to get the OfNat instance for N. It could in fact just as well be a def:

def N : Type := Nat

def thirtyNine : N := (39 : Nat)

Side note: to get around the ascription, one could use deriving:

def N : Type := Nat
deriving OfNat

def thirtyNine : N := 39

But the explanation "defining the new name for Nat using abbrev instead of def allows overloading resolution to replace the defined name with its definition. Definitions written using abbrev are always unfolded" suggests that Lean is doing some kind of "unfolding" in the example, which seems incorrect to me -- or maybe I have understood how abbreviations work completely wrong.

Can anyone point me to resources or explain when to use abbreviations over a regular def?

The unfolding that the text alludes to happens at the beginning of type class resolution. When you make a type class query for OfNat N Lean is going to unfold abbreviations in that query so you will instead make a query for OfNat Nat which is solved directly. The general idea is that you use an abbrev when you just want to inherit all available type class instances automatically and don't care about defining your own.
